content.thinking: The user is asking how to design a fault-tolerant retry strategy for an HTTP client. Let me think through the design space: (1) exponential backoff with jitter is well-established; (2) circuit-breaker pattern complements retry to avoid hammering a downed backend; (3) idempotency keys are essential for non-idempotent verbs; (4) budget caps (max retries x max elapsed time) prevent runaway loops. I should also consider partial-failure semantics and observability - every retry needs structured logging so on-call can trace the cascade.

content.text: A solid retry strategy has four pillars: exponential backoff with jitter, a circuit breaker, idempotency keys, and a budget cap. Combine them and your client degrades gracefully instead of cascading.
